Raahil Muhammad
Wildan.

I’m a cybersecurity student who tests web applications and APIs. I’m especially interested in what happens when a request reaches the wrong part of a system.

Before I started hunting bugs, I worked in a data center and taught routing. I still think in terms of a request’s journey. Where does it go? Which service decides what the user can see? If I find myself checking the same thing twice, I’ll usually write a small tool for it.

One bug I reported started with a feature that fetched pictures. It turned out the server could read a local file, too. My writeup walks through how I confirmed the impact and what the team could change to prevent it.
